feature: Width and Caps on every outline, and an icon's first outline
summary: Every outline now says Width and Caps, with Caps as the words Butt, Round and Square. Turning the outline on for a path in an icon starts it at 1.75, Center and round, so its SVG is one stroked path with no clip path.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Window about 1000 points tall. The walk is path-outline-width-caps-walk.

try.do: Choose New Frame, pick 24 under Icons, and draw an ellipse and a rectangle that overlap in it.
Pick both and choose Union from the Layers menu.
Tick the Outline row in Appearance.
Type 2.5 into Width and press Return.
Press Dashed under Pattern, then click Square under Caps.
Draw an open path in the frame with the Pen and click Butt under Caps.
Draw a line on the canvas and pick it: it says the same Width and Caps.
Compare the panel with the mock's Stroke section.

evaluate: Does a first outline of 1.75 look right on your icons, or should it match the 2 a Pen line starts at?
Is Butt clear enough, with its tip, for someone who only redlines screenshots?
With Columns and Layout going below the fold, is Appearance now the right thing to keep whole?
Is it fine that switching an icon's outline off and on starts it at 1.75, Center and round again?
rough: Width stays a slider with a typed number where the mock draws a dropdown of weights, as card a-drawn-path-s-outline-settings-read-like-the-ic-the-icon-mock-calls-a-path-s-lin answered.

Caps stays hidden on a closed solid path where the mock always shows it, as card a-drawn-path-s-outline-settings-read-like-the-ic-the-icon-mock-calls-a-path-s-lin answered: it would change nothing on the canvas.
The mock's Stroke section is an Outline row here, your call on 2026-09-06.

The mock's note under Stroke, that the weight is saved as a style and every glyph follows it, is left out because no saved stroke exists yet: task a-glyph-takes-the-icon-set-s-saved-stroke-in-one covers it.
Pattern and Corners go further than the mock. Pattern sits above Caps so that pressing Dashed does not move the row under the pointer.
A pull on the Width slider still lands on whole points. Only a typed number keeps a fraction.
A Pen line in an icon still starts at 2 while an outline starts at 1.75, so one icon can hold both weights until you set them.
Switching an icon's outline off and on again resets Align, Corners and Caps, because nothing records whether they were chosen by hand.
On an arrow, Width and Caps stay under Advanced, and that block can need a scroll inside Appearance.
A component's number knob and the Current release keep the word Thickness.
